title: Doctoral research: UAV cybersecurity
statusNote: State precisely, e.g. doctoral candidate, dissertation in progress, defended (year), or published (venue). Do not describe unpublished work as published.
question: How can structured threat intelligence, extended for unmanned aerial systems, be combined with streaming telemetry and network evidence to detect and explain cyberattacks against UAV operations?
environment: Software-in-the-loop flight stack (ArduPilot or PX4) with a ground control station
Simulated network carrying MAVLink traffic, monitored by Suricata and Zeek
Scripted attack injection with recorded ground truth
architecture: STIX 2.1 objects for UAV assets, observables, indicators, and attack patterns
Knowledge graph linking intelligence objects, detections, and ATT&CK techniques
Streaming detectors that emit graph-linked findings
methodology: Define attack scenarios such as GPS spoofing, MAVLink command injection, and telemetry disruption
Run each scenario and matched benign flights in simulation
Score detection and attribution against injector ground truth
stix: Custom STIX extensions for UAV-specific assets and telemetry observables
Mapping of UAV attack behaviors to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, noting gaps where no technique fits
measures: Detection rate and false positives per flight hour
interests: Threat intelligence for cyber-physical and autonomous systems
Evaluation methods for agentic and retrieval systems
Multimodal evidence fusion for security investigations
Provenance and auditability in AI-assisted decisions
